To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
supplementation with ALC and LA improves learning in aged dogs on two tasks that assess spatial and non‐spatial learning, but not on a task that assesses working memory.
supplementation with ALC and LA for ~2 months improved learning in two landmark‐based discrimination tasks in aged dogs.

(1) Aged dogs given a twice daily supplement for ~2 months of LA and ALC made significantly fewer errors on a two‐landmark discrimination learning task and (2) Aged dogs administered the same twice daily supplement of LA + ALC over ~2 months also made significantly fewer errors than controls on a two‐object discrimination learning task.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a model system for the study of aging in the dog.
the development of an effective, non‐toxic and inexpensive treatment that can improve the quality of life for aging dogs and humans.
the effects of dietary supplementation with acetyl‐L‐Carnitine and/or alpha‐L‐lipoic Acid on the performance of aged dogs on two different types of spatial learning tasks.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the results from this study suggest that long‐ term maintenance on LA and/or ALC may be beneficial in improving learning in aged dogs and that further study is warranted to evaluate the effects of this treatment on other aspects of cognitive functioning and to determine whether the effects of this supplement are sustained with long‐ term use.
ALC and LA supplementation of aged dogs improved learning in two landmark tasks, and that these improvements are likely to reflect a slowing of age‐related mitochondrial decay and/or cellular aging.
the study was well designed and the results are convincing.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the combination of ALA and ALC supplementation can improve learning and memory in older beagle dogs, and this improvement is not due to increased motor activity.

we found that supplementation with ALC and LA in aged dogs improved their performance on two different types of learning tasks, and that the effect was not due to an increase in motor activity or motivation.

we showed that the combination of LA and ALC improved spatial learning in aged dogs and that the effect was not due to a change in motivation to perform the task, as assessed by the number of trials taken to reach the criterion on a variable delay spatial task.
The main takeaway from our work is that
acetyl‐l-carnitine and alpha‐lipoic aid supplementation of dogs over the age of 8 years old can improve cognitive function in the short-term.
the supplement is effective in improving discrimination and learning in dogs.
the use of LA and ALC in combination can help improve learning.
